newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian firm sees good prospects in Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian firm sees good prospects in Kazakhstan.

text.p: Indonesian businessman Setiawan Djody, who owns fifty percent of Central Asia Petroleum Ltd, said on Tuesday that there were good prospects for developing the giant Mangistaumunaigaz oil field in Kazakhstan.

"The oil prospects are good in Kazakhstan as the potential is there. Based on the data we have, we believe the reserves are in large amounts," Djody, the chairman of the privately-owned Setdco Group and Central Asia Petroleum, told Reuters.
He was reacting to news that Central Asia Petroleum signed an agreement on Monday to buy a 60 percent stake in Kazakhstan's largest oil company Mangistaumunaigaz for a total of $4.348 billion.
"I confirm the reports that we are involved in Kazakhstan's major oil company," he said.
He said the other 50 percent of Central Asia Petroleum was held by Arifin Panigoro, the president commisioner of PT Medco Energy Corp.
Djody said he saw no problem in financing the oil project although he gave no details.
"We have signed so there must be no problem (in financing). We have carefully calculated (the cost)," he said.
He said Setdco was not new to the oil business, in which it had been involved since the 1980s.
Djody said other interests of the group included hotels, shipping, telecommunications and property.
He said Mangistaumunaigaz produces about 95,000 barrels per day of crude oil and production will be doubled in around five years time.
He said the crude will be marketed in Europe.
Mangistaumunaigaz is located in the west of the Central Asian state and is its largest oil company. Last year it produced only four million tonnes of oil.

In Soviet times oil production at Mangistaumunaigaz, which sits on reserves estimated at 200 million tonnes, peaked at 25 million tonnes per year which is equivalent to Kazakhstan's current annual oil output.
